To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the immunological synaptosomes of NK cells, iNKT cells and CTLs all have secretory clefts and docked centrioles within the synapse.

the centrosomes in NK and iNTK cells are polarised towards the plasma membrane within immunological synapses and this polarisation is accompanied by polarisation of the Golgi and recycling endosomes towards the centrosomes, as well as secretory lysosomes polarising along microtubule tracks towards the docked (polarised) centrosomes.
centriole polarisation is a mechanism used by cytolytic cells from both the innate and the adaptive immune systems to direct the delivery of secretory lysosome exocytosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of cytolytic cell-mediated immune surveillance.
the mechanisms of polarised secretion of cytotoxic granules in cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) cells, a key component of the cellular immune response.

understanding how cytolytic cells deliver secretory lysosomes (containing perforin and granzyme) precisely to the point at which they are to be released from the cytolytic cell, and how this is achieved by the polarisation of the centrosomes towards the plasma membrane at this point of contact.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
centrosomal docking is a general mechanism for directing secretory lysosomes towards the immunological synase in cytolytic cells.
polarised secretion from cytolyic cells is directed by centriole polarisation towards the immunological synapase, which is common to CTL, NK cells and NKT cells of the immune systems.
the centrosome provides a mechanism of polarised secretion for cytolytic cells in both the adaptive and innate immune systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the centrosome plays a central role in the delivery of secretory vesicles to the immunological (or NK) synapse.
centrioles are polarised to the plasma membrane within immunological synapses of both innate and adaptive cytotoxic cells.

polarised centriole docking to the plasma membrane within an immunological synapse is not restricted to CTLs of the immune system, but is also used by cytolytic cells in both the innate and the adaptive immune system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytolytic cells in the innate and adaptive arms of the immune system use the same mechanism to deliver their lethal hits.
centrosomes are important organelles that can polarise to direct secretion and endocytotic processes in immune cells.
the centrosome is a central player in polarising the immunological synapsis in all cytolytic cells.
